name: Jeffrey B. Peltz, P.C.
about: Jeffrey B. Peltz works from Broadway and practises divorce alongside bankruptcy, immigration and real estate, which its own title says. It explains twelve stages of a matrimonial case, the most of any firm in this ranking, from the summons and the net worth statement to the attorney for the child and the judgment.

212 reviews at 4.9, and twenty-eight years by its domain registration, the longest history here. Its own pages name no attorney we could read. Hospital visits and pages in Spanish, published, and nothing about the rate or the retainer.

summons.quote: The plaintiff commences the divorce action by buying an index number from the county clerk for $210 and by filing a summons with notice.

net worth statement.quote: The financial net worth statement is extensive and must include all of each party’s assets and liabilities.

preliminary conference.quote: In New York, the first hearing before the judge is known as the preliminary conference, also known as the PC.

discovery.quote: At the preliminary conference, the judge will direct that discovery, which is the exchange of financial and other information, take place between the parties and will set deadlines.

equitable distribution.quote: Such terms may include spousal support , which was formerly known as alimony; equitable distribution , which refers to the division of property and other assets; child custody; visitation and child support .

trial.quote: The next step in a contested divorce in New York is the completion of discovery, the payment of the note of issue , which costs $30, and the scheduling of the trial.

judgment.quote: When the judge signs the judgment of divorce, it is entered at the county clerk, at which point the parties are officially divorced.

settlement.quote: The first, and by far the most common way is for the spouses to enter into a legal separation agreement.

attorney for the child.quote: If both parents want custody, the court will appoint a law guardian to represent the child.
